question: What consensus algorithm does Stellar use, and how is it different from Proof-of-Work or Proof-of-Stake?

golden.answer: Stellar uses the Stellar Consensus Protocol (SCP), a Federated Byzantine Agreement construction in which each node picks the quorum sets it trusts. It needs no mining hashpower (Proof-of-Work) or staked capital (Proof-of-Stake), and validators earn no block rewards. SCP favors safety over liveness: it can halt rather than fork.
keyFacts: Stellar uses SCP, a Federated Byzantine Agreement construction.
Agreement comes from user-defined quorum sets, not mining hashpower or staked capital.
SCP favors safety over liveness and pays no validator block rewards.
avoid: Do NOT say Stellar uses Proof-of-Work, Proof-of-Stake, PBFT or Tendermint.
